site.name: Arkansas County, Arkansas
site.note: Grand Prairie rice and soybean on a clay-pan soil. Humid where every other field here is semi-arid, and flooded exactly the way Punjab is - which is what lets the paddy water balance be checked against an observed record for the first time.

terrain.note: no DEM tile downloaded for this site, so the slope-length factor uses a placeholder of 0.25; the erosion figure here is indicative only

region.name: US Mid-South
region.yield_validation: USDA NASS: county rice yields from 1938, and state irrigation water applied to rice (2013, 2018, 2023) - the only observed record we have found anywhere against which the ponded paddy water balance can be checked directly
review_first: Percolation under the permanent flood, declared at 2.0 mm/day against Punjab's 4.0. The Grand Prairie is rice country precisely because a dense clay subsoil holds water, so a lower figure is expected - but it is the single number the irrigation estimate turns on and it is swept rather than asserted in scripts/validate_paddy.py.

Flood timing, now modelled as a window rather than the whole season - dry from drilling to about the four-leaf stage, flooded for 95 days, drained before harvest. Correcting this was the first thing the Arkansas test demanded; it did NOT close the gap, which is what sent the search to crop water use instead.
region.note: Grand Prairie rice and soybean on a clay-pan soil. Humid where every other field we run is semi-arid, and flooded exactly as Punjab is - which is what makes the paddy model testable here.

objectives.label: production (dry matter)
objectives.note: summed as dry matter, because marketed weight cannot be added across crops holding different amounts of water - 25 t/ha of potato is about 5 t/ha of dry matter. Becomes margin when local prices are supplied.

objectives.label: production in a bad year
objectives.note: tenth percentile across simulated years for THIS FIELD, including years it produces nothing. A farmer staggering the rotation across several fields sees a steadier farm-level income; compare with production for that view.

objectives.label: irrigation demand
objectives.note: at the field gate, including application losses; the binding constraint where groundwater is declining

objectives.label: soil carbon change
objectives.note: RothC over the simulated period, 0-23 cm

objectives.label: wind erosion exposure
objectives.note: ordinal, for comparing rotations at one site; not a mass flux

objectives.label: bare ground
objectives.note: the clearest single explanation behind carbon loss and erosion exposure
